title: THAD PROFILE WALK CONTINUITY -- owner-authorized global character art revision (Tyler, 2026-09-05)

sourceUsable.why: true side profile, walking right, leading leg forward and trailing leg back with clear key between them on 337 of 453 lower rows, both arms clear of the torso on 230 of 396 arm rows, hands free of the coat, boots separated, coat hem a clean edge at 68% of height, no twist toward camera, 12% margins on every side, flat #FF00FF backdrop. Head, hair, coat and proportions read as the standing still.

rig.chosenFromVariants: swing 1.0/knee 0, 0.7/0, 0.7/0.5, 0.5/0 laid out at one height; 0.7/0 chosen: readable stride, boots within 5 px of the ground line across the cycle, no kick, no shuffle

downscale.py: resample premultiplied planes in float (byte rounding before the resize came back as purple edge pixels after un-premultiplying) and despill Lanczos ringing to eight under the fringe line

secondCut.why: Tyler (2026-09-05): 'The side profile is way better but Thad now gallops instead of looking like he's walking.' Cause: character.py added its hip sine to the source's OWN stride, so the legs opened wider and closed with the same leg leading every frame (a five-picture bound). No image operation: same source, the rig corrected.
rigChanges: --level-limbs: each limb's source angle measured (near leg +21.8, far leg -19.9, far arm -13.9, near arm +1.4 degrees from vertical) and subtracted, all legs swung about one hip column, so frame 0 leads with the near leg and frame 4 with the far leg
grounding: every frame dropped so its lowest sole meets the cycle's own ground row; the head bobs (up to 17 px on the 625 figure, 2.7%) at double support instead of the feet floating
downscale.py: despill applied after the clip to the byte range (one ringing pixel came back pure red)
secondCut.variantsCompared: levelled swing 1.0 / 1.3 / 1.5 (steps 138 / 169 / 194 px on 625; 3.7 / 3.0 / 2.6 steps a second at pace 1.0) and 1.0 with knee 0.5; 1.5 matches the source's own +/-21 degree stride and walks rather than patters

cadence.why: one cycle is now two steps (contralateral half); 2 x 194 px sole separation on the 625 figure = 149 px at 240. Cycles/s = 194 x pace / 149: 1.3 at A, 1.63 at B, 1.95 at C; steps/s 2.6 / 3.25 / 3.9. Translation semantics untouched: walkSpeed, its height scaling and ?pace= are as before.

thirdCut.why: Tyler (2026-09-05): 'his back arm stays up at about waist height while his front arm stays at his side... a weird dance move'. Cause: the source's forward arm is bent at the elbow; split_arms lifts only the part of an arm clear of the coat's silhouette, which for that arm is the forearm alone, a slab attached by its upper end to the coat at waist height; levelled and swung about its own centre, its hand stayed at the waist front to back. The rear arm is a hanging strip and swung only a little, so it read as still.
rigChanges: each lifted arm is its largest connected piece; the one- or two-pixel coat-edge slivers the split left on it go back to the coat (they had been the arm's "farthest pixel" and set its angle)

each arm hangs from its ATTACHMENT to the coat (centroid of the pixels touching the coat): its angle from vertical there is taken out (rear arm -12.8, forearm +33.8), and it swings about the shoulder above the attachment, so both arms hang at his sides and swing in opposition

fourthCut.why: Tyler (2026-09-05): 'You can see where you made cuts in his arms, so they now look partially disconnected from his body at the elbows... dangling parts of limbs that were severed.' Cause: a lifted arm piece rotated about its own cut edge opens a wedge at the cut, and the third cut rotated each arm 13-34 degrees there.
fourthCut.rigChange: the legs' own recipe applied to the arms: each piece is levelled about its attachment, then EXTENDED up to the shoulder by repeating its top rows (the near sleeve continuing to the coat's shoulder over the coat, the far forearm's upper end under it), then swung about the shoulder, so the join sits at a real joint and the rotation there moves the joined rows by almost nothing

intactCut.why: Tyler rejected the fourth cut (2026-09-05): the arm joins still failed in live play -- detached, severed, an extra limb, a floating forearm. Ruling: stop the cut-arm -> extend -> rotate method; the profile upper body, coat, shoulders and arms stay one intact authored silhouette while walking.
intactCut.whyArticulationAbandoned: four cuts of puppet-style arm articulation each moved the seam rather than removing it: a piece cut from the coat and rotated shows its cut, and a piece extended to hide the cut shows the extension. At gameplay scale the walk is judged on continuity, not on arm swing.

upperBodySource.note: the approved standing frame the game already draws; its pixels are unchanged, so stand -> walk -> stand shares one upper body

intactCut.legMethod: character.py --legs-only --level-limbs (swing 1.5, knee 0) from the stride source: the two legs levelled so they alternate, swung about one hip column, grounded; downscaled by the stand's own factor (tools/rig/downscale.py --factor 0.5365); set under the coat by tools/rig/intact-walk.py with their soles on the stand's ground row and their hip column under the coat's centre; the stride coat's hem band and cast shadow on the thighs recoloured column by column from clean trouser rows (shapes kept); one per-channel gain matches the trousers to the stand's; the upper body drops by the frame's ground shift (up to 9 px on 625) so the whole man bobs
